title: Compounds and Chemical Reactions
summary: Name compounds and write their formulae, represent reactions with word and balanced equations, and understand the conservation of atoms and mass.

notes.text: A **compound** is a substance made of two or more different elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio. A **chemical formula** shows which elements are present and how many atoms of each are in one unit of the compound.

items: For a compound of a metal and a non-metal, name the metal first, then change the ending of the non-metal to **-ide**: sodium + chlorine → sodium chlor**ide**; iron + sulfur → iron sulf**ide**; magnesium + oxygen → magnesium ox**ide**.
**-ate** endings mean the compound also contains oxygen: calcium carbon**ate** (CaCO₃), copper sulf**ate** (CuSO₄).
Prefixes show the number of atoms: **mono-** (1), **di-** (2), **tri-** (3): carbon **mon**oxide (CO), carbon **di**oxide (CO₂).

notes.text: A **word equation** names the reactants and products. A **balanced chemical equation** uses formulae and has the same number of each type of atom on both sides.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: To balance an equation, change only the **big numbers in front** of formulae (coefficients). Never change the small subscript numbers, because that would change the substance.

notes.title: Balancing an equation
steps: Count atoms. Left: 2 H, 2 O. Right: 2 H, 1 O. Oxygen is not balanced.
Put a 2 in front of H₂O: H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Now right: 4 H, 2 O.
Hydrogen is now unbalanced, so put a 2 in front of H₂: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
Check: left 4 H, 2 O; right 4 H, 2 O ✓

notes.title: Counting atoms with coefficients
notes.problem: How many oxygen atoms are in 3CO₂?

notes.text: Atoms are rearranged during a reaction, but none are created or destroyed. Therefore **the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products**. If a gas is produced in an open container, the container seems to lose mass because the gas escapes.
**Exothermic reactions** give out heat (burning, respiration); **endothermic reactions** take in heat (photosynthesis, thermal decomposition of limestone).

questions.prompt: Name the compound with the formula NaCl.

How many atoms in total are in one unit of CaCO₃?
How many hydrogen atoms are in 2NH₃?

✓ Check: 2 Mg and 2 O on each side (1)

questions.prompt: Marble chips react with acid in an open flask on a balance. The reading on the balance decreases. Does this disprove conservation of mass? Explain.
questions.memo:
